question: A team is auditing which hook events in their guardrail configuration are actually capable of stopping an unwanted action, as opposed to merely observing or logging it after the fact. Which of the following hook events can block or otherwise prevent the associated action from proceeding, per Anthropic's documentation? (Select 3)
options: A) Notification, which can return decision: block to suppress a status message before it fires
B) UserPromptSubmit, which can return decision: block to erase the prompt before Claude processes it
C) PostToolUse, which can return permissionDecision: deny to undo a tool call after it completes
D) FileChanged, which can return permissionDecision: deny to stop a watched file from being modified on disk
E) PreToolUse, which can return permissionDecision: deny to stop a tool call before it runs
F) Stop, which can return decision: block to prevent Claude from ending its turn
correct_answers: B) UserPromptSubmit, which can return decision: block to erase the prompt before Claude processes it
E) PreToolUse, which can return permissionDecision: deny to stop a tool call before it runs
F) Stop, which can return decision: block to prevent Claude from ending its turn
explanations: Incorrect. Notification only reports status events like permission prompts; it has no documented decision field that blocks the notification or any underlying action.
Correct. UserPromptSubmit fires before Claude processes the prompt, and decision: block erases it so Claude never sees it.
Incorrect. PostToolUse fires after the tool call has already succeeded; there is no documented permissionDecision on PostToolUse, and it cannot undo an already-completed action.
Incorrect. FileChanged fires after a watched file has already changed on disk; it observes the change rather than gating a permissionDecision before the modification occurs.
Correct. PreToolUse fires before execution and permissionDecision: deny stops the tool call from ever running.
Correct. Stop fires when Claude finishes responding, and decision: block prevents the stop, continuing the conversation instead.
